items.title: Coverage error under score, forward-solver, and finite-time error
items.statement:
Fix integers $d,n\ge1$, parameters $p,s,a,R,\sigma>0$, a credibility error $\gamma\in(0,1)$, and a continuous schedule $\beta:[0,T]\to(0,\infty)$ with $T>0$. Let
$$\Theta_s(R)=\left\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d:\sum_{j=1}^d j^{2s}\theta_j^2\le R^2\right\},\qquad A_p=\operatorname{diag}(1^{-p},2^{-p},\ldots,d^{-p}).$$
Observe $Y_i=A_p\theta+\varepsilon_i$, $1\le i\le n$, with independent $\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2 I_d)$. Use the proper Gaussian prior $\Pi_0=N(0,\operatorname{diag}(j^{-1-2a})_{j=1}^d)$, and let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid Y)$ be its exact posterior under the stated forward operator and noise law. Let $m_n(Y)$ be the posterior mean and let $r_{n,\gamma}(Y)$ be the unique radius for which the Euclidean ball
$$C_{n,\gamma}(Y)=\{u\in\mathbb R^d:\|u-m_n(Y)\|_2\le r_{n,\gamma}(Y)\}$$
has posterior probability $1-\gamma$. Define the exact frequentist coverage $c_{n,\gamma}(\theta)=P_{n,\theta}\{\theta\in C_{n,\gamma}(Y)\}$ and its baseline error $\delta^0_{n,\gamma}=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s(R)}|c_{n,\gamma}(\theta)-(1-\gamma)|$.

For a deterministic numerical matrix $\widehat A_n\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ with $\delta_A\ge0$ and $\|\widehat A_n-A_p\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_A$, let $\widehat\Pi_n(\cdot\mid Y)$ be the Gaussian posterior formed with $\widehat A_n$ and the same prior and noise variance. Write $\widehat p_{n,t}^Y$ for the density obtained by applying the forward variance-preserving diffusion $dX_t=-\tfrac12\beta(t)X_t\,dt+\sqrt{\beta(t)}\,dW_t$ to $X_0\sim\widehat\Pi_n(\cdot\mid Y)$, and set $\widehat s_{n,t}^Y=\nabla\log\widehat p_{n,t}^Y$. A jointly Borel learned score field $s_{n,t}^Y$ is required to satisfy
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s(R)}E_{Y\sim P_{n,\theta}}\left[\frac1T\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb R^d}\|s_{n,t}^Y(x)-\widehat s_{n,t}^Y(x)\|_2^2\widehat p_{n,t}^Y(x)\,dx\,dt\right]\le\varepsilon_s^2.$$
For $h=T/K$, define the reverse-time Euler chain by $Z_0\sim\widehat p_{n,T}^Y$ and, for $k=0,\ldots,K-1$,
$$Z_{k+1}=Z_k+h\left[\tfrac12\beta(T-kh)Z_k+\beta(T-kh)s_{n,T-kh}^Y(Z_k)\right]+\sqrt{h\beta(T-kh)}\,\zeta_k,$$
where the $\zeta_k$ are independent $N(0,I_d)$ vectors independent of $Z_0$ and the observations. Draw $M$ independent copies of this chain conditionally on $Y$ and denote their terminal values by $X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(M)}$. Let $\bar X=M^{-1}\sum_iX^{(i)}$, let $\widehat r$ be the empirical $1-\gamma$ quantile of $\{\|X^{(i)}-\bar X\|_2\}_{i=1}^M$ (the smallest order statistic whose empirical cumulative mass is at least $1-\gamma$), and put $\widehat C_{n,K,M}(Y)=\{u:\|u-\bar X\|_2\le\widehat r\}$. Suppose the exact credible-ball boundary satisfies the uniform margin condition
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s(R)}P_{n,\theta}\left(\left|\|\theta-m_n(Y)\|_2-r_{n,\gamma}(Y)\right|\le u\right)\le C_{\mathrm{ac}}u^\kappa\quad(0<u\le u_0)$$
for fixed $C_{\mathrm{ac}},u_0>0$ and $\kappa>0$. Determine whether a minimax-sharp nonasymptotic function $\Phi$ exists uniformly over all such score fields and, if it does, find it as a function of $d,n,p,s,a,R,\sigma,T,\gamma,C_{\mathrm{ac}},u_0,\kappa,\delta_A,\varepsilon_s,K^{-1}$, and $M^{-1/2}$ such that
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_s(R)}\left|P_{n,\theta,\mathrm{sampler}}\{\theta\in\widehat C_{n,K,M}(Y)\}-(1-\gamma)\right|\le\delta^0_{n,\gamma}+\Phi,$$
with matching lower bounds that identify when $\Phi\to0$. The probability includes observation noise and sampler randomness. The target concerns the additional coverage error introduced by the approximate forward operator, learned score, finite reverse discretization, and finite posterior sample; it does not assume that the exact Bayesian credible ball is already calibrated on every truth class.

items.title: Joint sample and mesh rates for neural inverse maps
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ carry normalized Lebesgue measure and fix the real orthonormal Fourier basis
$$\phi_1(x)=1,\qquad \phi_{2k}(x)=\sqrt2\cos(kx),\qquad \phi_{2k+1}(x)=\sqrt2\sin(kx)\quad(k\ge1).$$
Use this basis to identify the real Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with $L^2(\mathbb T;\mathbb R)$. Fix integers $N,m\ge1$ and parameters $s,p,R,\sigma>0$, and define
$$\Theta_s(R)=\left\{\theta\in\ell^2:\sum_{j\ge1}j^{2s}\theta_j^2\le R^2\right\},\qquad (A_p\theta)_j=j^{-p}\theta_j,\qquad \mathcal X_p(R)=A_p\Theta_s(R).$$
The inverse map $G^\dagger:\mathcal X_p(R)\to\ell^2$ is $G^\dagger(A_p\theta)=\theta$. For $m\ge1$, let $P_m$ retain the first $m$ Fourier coefficients and let $I_m:\mathbb R^m\to\ell^2$ append zero coordinates.

Fix a globally Lipschitz nonpolynomial function $\sigma_0:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, called the activation. For $x\in\mathbb R^m$, form the scalar input field $\bar u_0(x;z)=\sum_{j=1}^m x_j\phi_j(z)$. A pointwise affine lift $u_0(x;z)=V_{\mathrm{in}}\bar u_0(x;z)+b_{\mathrm{in}}$, with $V_{\mathrm{in}}\in\mathbb R^{c_0}$ and $b_{\mathrm{in}}\in\mathbb R^{c_0}$, creates $c_0$ channels. For fields $u_\ell(z)\in\mathbb R^{c_\ell}$ with positive integer channel counts $c_\ell$, apply an integer number $D\ge1$ of layers indexed by $\ell=0,\ldots,D-1$:
$$u_{\ell+1}(z)=\sigma_0\!\left(W_\ell u_\ell(z)+b_\ell+(\mathcal K_\ell u_\ell)(z)\right).$$
Here $\sigma_0$ acts coordinatewise, $W_\ell\in\mathbb R^{c_{\ell+1}\times c_\ell}$ and $b_\ell\in\mathbb R^{c_{\ell+1}}$ are pointwise channel weights, and $\mathcal K_\ell$ is a Fourier multiplier meaning $\widehat{(\mathcal K_\ell u)}(k)=R_{\ell,k}\widehat u(k)$, where $\widehat u(k)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}u(z)e^{-ikz}\,dz$ is computed componentwise, with matrices $R_{\ell,k}\in\mathbb C^{c_{\ell+1}\times c_\ell}$ satisfying $R_{\ell,-k}=\overline{R_{\ell,k}}$ and $R_{\ell,k}=0$ for $|k|>q$ for some integer cutoff $q\ge0$. A pointwise affine output map $v(x;z)=a_{\mathrm{out}}^\top u_D(z)+b_{\mathrm{out}}$ gives a real scalar field, and the network output is $\Psi_m(x)=(\langle v(x;\cdot),\phi_j\rangle_{L^2})_{j=1}^m$. Let $\mathcal F_{S,B}^{(m)}$ be the union of these maps over architectures whose depth, channel counts, Fourier cutoff, and number of real scalar parameters are each at most the integer $S\ge1$, with every trainable parameter bounded in absolute value by $B>0$. A parameter array used at mesh size $m$ is the same array at every other mesh size. For fixed $S$, there are finitely many allowed architecture indices; equip their disjoint union of bounded real parameter boxes with its Borel structure.

Write $\mathcal P(K)$ for the Borel probability laws on a Borel set $K$. For a Borel probability law $\mu$ on $\Theta_s(R)$, draw independent training truths $\theta_i\sim\mu$ and observations
$$X_{i,m}=P_mA_p\theta_i+\eta_{i,m},\qquad Y_{i,m}=P_m\theta_i,\qquad \eta_{i,m}\sim N(0,\sigma^2m^{-1}I_m),\quad i=1,\ldots,N,$$
with all noises independent, and write $D_{N,m}=((X_{i,m},Y_{i,m}))_{i=1}^N$. A selector is Borel into the finite disjoint union of architecture indices and their bounded parameter boxes, and its realized map minimizes the empirical loss. For each $N,m,S,B$, assume there is at least one such selector $\tau$ that, from $D_{N,m}$, returns a minimizer of
$$\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\|\Psi(X_{i,m})-Y_{i,m}\|_2^2$$
over $\Psi\in\mathcal F_{S,B}^{(m)}$; let $\mathcal T_{N,m}(S,B)$ be the set of all such selectors. At test time, draw an independent $\theta\sim\mu$ and $\eta_m\sim N(0,\sigma^2m^{-1}I_m)$, and define
$$\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{ERM}}_{N,m}(S,B)=\inf_{\tau\in\mathcal T_{N,m}(S,B)}\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal P(\Theta_s(R))}E\left\|I_m\tau(D_{N,m})(P_mA_p\theta+\eta_m)-\theta\right\|_{\ell^2}^2.$$
Also define $\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{all}}_{N,m}$ by the same infimum over all Borel predictors from $(D_{N,m},X_m)$ to $\mathbb R^m$, with $X_m=P_mA_p\theta+\eta_m$. Determine matching minimax upper and lower rates for $\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{ERM}}_{N,m}(S,B)$ jointly in $N,m,S,B,p,s,R,\sigma$. In particular, characterize the joint growth regimes of $m=m_N$ and $S=S_N$ that separate statistical estimation, neural-operator approximation, and continuum truncation error, and determine when the bounded shared-parameter Fourier architecture attains the unrestricted rate $\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{all}}_{N,m}$.

title: Open frontiers in calibrated and robust learned inversion — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Exact Gaussian credible-ball coverage with a score-error budget of zero
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $\sigma,\tau>0$, and $0<\gamma<1$. Given a scalar truth $\theta\in\mathbb R$, observe independent $Y_i\sim N(\theta,\sigma^2)$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, and use the proper prior $\theta\sim N(0,\tau^2)$. Write $\bar Y=n^{-1}\sum_iY_i$, $v_n=(\tau^{-2}+n\sigma^{-2})^{-1}$, $a_n=v_n n\sigma^{-2}$, and $z_\gamma=\Phi^{-1}(1-\gamma/2)$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The exact posterior is $N(a_n\bar Y,v_n)$ and its central $(1-\gamma)$ credible interval is $C_n(\bar Y)=[a_n\bar Y-z_\gamma\sqrt{v_n},a_n\bar Y+z_\gamma\sqrt{v_n}]$. Its frequentist coverage at truth $\theta$ is
$$P_\theta\{\theta\in C_n(\bar Y)\}=\Phi\!\left(\frac{z_\gamma\sqrt{v_n}+(1-a_n)\theta}{a_n\sigma/\sqrt n}\right)-\Phi\!\left(\frac{-z_\gamma\sqrt{v_n}+(1-a_n)\theta}{a_n\sigma/\sqrt n}\right).$$
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all distributions are finite-dimensional and explicit.

items.title: A proper Gaussian prior gives nonuniform finite-sample coverage on an unbounded truth class
items.statement: Fix $n\ge1$, $\sigma,\tau>0$, and $0<\gamma<1$. Observe independent $Y_i\sim N(\theta,\sigma^2)$ under truth $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and use prior $N(0,\tau^2)$. Let $v_n=(\tau^{-2}+n\sigma^{-2})^{-1}$, $a_n=v_n n\sigma^{-2}$, and $z_\gamma=\Phi^{-1}(1-\gamma/2)$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The exact posterior credible interval is $[a_n\bar Y-z_\gamma\sqrt{v_n},a_n\bar Y+z_\gamma\sqrt{v_n}]$. Since $0<a_n<1$, its repeated-sampling coverage at fixed $n$ tends to zero as $|\theta|\to\infty$, despite exact posterior computation and exact sampling.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the scalar Gaussian model and limits are explicit.

items.title: A scalar inverse with a conditioning-dependent shift modulus
items.statement:
Fix $R,a_0,\sigma>0$ and $0\le\rho_A<a_0/2$. The working inverse is $g(y)=y/a_0$. Under a test operator $a=a_0+\delta$ with $|\delta|\le\rho_A$, the observation is $Y=a\theta+\varepsilon$ for $\theta\in[-R,R]$ and independent $\varepsilon\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$. For any two truth laws $\mu_0,\mu$ on $[-R,R]$, define $W_1(\mu,\mu_0)$ as the infimum of $E|\Theta-\Theta_0|$ over their couplings. The risk is
$$R_{\mu,\delta}(g)=E_{\theta\sim\mu,\varepsilon}|g((a_0+\delta)\theta+\varepsilon)-\theta|^2=\frac{\delta^2}{a_0^2}E_\mu\theta^2+\frac{\sigma^2}{a_0^2},$$
and it satisfies $R_{\mu,\delta}(g)\le(\rho_A^2R^2+\sigma^2)/a_0^2$ and
$$|R_{\mu,\delta}(g)-R_{\mu_0,\delta}(g)|\le\frac{2\delta^2R}{a_0^2}W_1(\mu,\mu_0).$$
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the scalar laws and couplings are explicit.

items.title: Small absolute operator error does not give a uniform inverse bound without conditioning
items.statement: Fix a truth bound $R>0$. For every absolute operator-shift radius $\rho_A>0$, take the working scalar operator $A_0=\rho_A/2$, the true operator $A=0$, the noiseless datum $Y=A\theta$ at truth $\theta=R$, and the working inverse $g(y)=y/A_0$. Then $|A-A_0|=\rho_A/2\le\rho_A$ but $|g(Y)-\theta|^2=R^2$. Thus no recovery modulus tending to zero with the absolute operator error can hold uniformly when the baseline inverse conditioning is allowed to vanish.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the scalar example is explicit.

items.title: Exact iid samples estimate two-mode posterior weights
items.statement:
Let $b>0$, $0<w<1$, and let the two-mode posterior be $\pi_w=w\delta_{-b}+(1-w)\delta_b$ on $\mathbb R$. From $M\ge1$ independent exact posterior draws $X_1,\ldots,X_M$, define $\widehat w=M^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i=-b\}$ and $\widehat\pi_M=\widehat w\delta_{-b}+(1-\widehat w)\delta_b$. The one-Wasserstein error and the probability that at least one posterior mode is absent from the sample are
$$W_1(\widehat\pi_M,\pi_w)=2b|\widehat w-w|,\qquad P\{\widehat w\in\{0,1\}\}=(1-w)^M+w^M,$$
and $E W_1(\widehat\pi_M,\pi_w)\le2b\sqrt{w(1-w)/M}$.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the two-point law and finite sample are explicit.

items.title: No fixed sample budget uniformly protects arbitrarily rare modes
items.statement: For the two-mode posterior $\pi_w=w\delta_{-b}+(1-w)\delta_b$ with $b>0$ and $0<w<1/2$, $M\ge1$ independent exact draws miss the rare mode $-b$ with probability $(1-w)^M$. For any fixed $M$, this probability tends to one as $w\downarrow0$. If instead $w\in[w_{\min},1-w_{\min}]$ with $0<w_{\min}\le1/2$, then the probability of missing either mode is at most $2(1-w_{\min})^M$, so $M\ge\log(2/\alpha)/[-\log(1-w_{\min})]$ suffices to make it at most $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the binomial sampling calculation is finite.

items.title: A diagonal inverse has an explicit Fourier truncation error
items.statement:
Let $p,s,R>0$, $m\ge1$, $\theta\in\ell^2$ satisfy $\sum_{j\ge1}j^{2s}\theta_j^2\le R^2$, and let $(A_p\theta)_j=j^{-p}\theta_j$. Given data $y=A_p\theta+\eta$ with $\|\eta\|_{\ell^2}\le\delta$, the mesh-$m$ truncated inverse is $g_m(y)=(j^py_j)_{j\le m}$ with zero output coordinates for $j>m$. It satisfies the continuum error bound
$$\|g_m(y)-\theta\|_{\ell^2}\le m^p\delta+R(m+1)^{-s}.$$
This separates measurement-noise amplification from the mesh truncation tail; it makes no statistical or neural-operator claim.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the truncation and norm estimates are explicit.

items.title: Finite samples cannot identify every Lipschitz inverse map uniformly
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ and let $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in[0,1]$ be arbitrary training inputs. For every deterministic learning rule that returns a prediction function $g:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ from the observed pairs $(x_i,f(x_i))$, there are two $1$-Lipschitz functions $f_0,f_1:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ agreeing with each other and taking the common value $0$ at every training input but satisfying
$$\|f_1-f_0\|_{\infty}\ge\frac{1}{2(N+1)}.$$
Consequently, at the midpoint of a largest sample-free interval, the returned prediction function $g$ has absolute prediction error at least $1/(4(N+1))$ for at least one of these two indistinguishable target functions.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the construction uses finitely many sample points.

items.statement: In the finite-dimensional Gaussian credible-ball question reproduced below, choose $d=n=1$, $R=1$, $\sigma=1$, $T=1$, $\beta(t)=1$, and $\gamma=1/4$, with arbitrary positive $p,s,a$. Take the numerical operator equal to the true operator, so $\delta_A=0$. For every integer $K\ge1$ there is a jointly Borel finite score field with integrated score error exactly zero, whose Euler terminal law is $N(1,K^{-1})$ for every observation. With $M=K$ independent terminal draws, the resulting empirical ball has frequentist coverage tending to zero at truth $\theta=0$, although the stated uniform boundary-margin condition holds with exponent $\kappa=1$. The exact credible-ball baseline satisfies $\delta^0_{1,1/4}<3/4$. Consequently no bound in that question can have $\Phi\to0$ uniformly over its original score class as $(\delta_A,\varepsilon_s,K^{-1},M^{-1/2})\to(0,0,0,0)$. The original formulation is retained verbatim under Original question.

items.statement:
For the robust minimax value $\mathfrak R_N(\rho_X,\rho_A)$ in the original question reproduced below, fix $p,s>0$, $R,\sigma>0$, $N\ge1$, $\rho_X\ge0$ and $0\le\rho_A<1/2$. Put
$$Q_{p,s}(R,\sigma)=R^2\min\left\{1,(\sigma/R)^{4s/(2s+2p+1)}\right\}.$$
There is $c_{p,s}>0$, depending only on $p,s$, such that
$$c_{p,s}\bigl(Q_{p,s}(R,\sigma)+R^2\rho_A^2\bigr)\le\mathfrak R_N(\rho_X,\rho_A)\le\min\left\{R^2,2Q_{p,s}(R,\sigma)+R^2\rho_A^2\right\}.$$
These bounds hold for every training size and truth-law shift radius. For fixed positive $p,s,R$, along any sequence of the remaining parameters the risk tends to zero if and only if both $\sigma\to0$ and $\rho_A\to0$. In particular, increasing $N$ with fixed positive noise does not force the worst-law risk to zero. The original question, including both distinct shift classes, is retained verbatim under Original question.

items.statement: For the separated-mixture question reproduced below, there are admissible fixed one-dimensional parameters with $L=2$, fixed positive score-error allowance $\varepsilon_s$, and every fixed integer $J\ge2$, for which the supremum of the displayed expected fidelity loss over the original finite-valued Borel score class is $+\infty$, for every finite $M\ge1$. Each individual field in the construction has a finite-first-moment Euler chain and obeys the required score bound at every time. Thus the original ideal-marginal $L^2$ hypothesis supplies no finite uniform bound for the requested loss, however large the fixed budget $JM$ is. The original question is retained verbatim under Original question.

items.statement:
Consider the complete original Fourier architecture and diagonal inverse question reproduced below. For every odd integer $m\ge3$, every $N\ge1$, and every admissible bounded parameter class with a measurable empirical minimizer, its risk satisfies
$$\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{ERM}}_{N,m}(S,B)\ge\frac{R^2(3^p-2^p)^2}{4\,3^{2(p+s)}}>0.$$
The same bound holds for every measurable learner whose realized predictor belongs to the stated coordinate-free Fourier class, whether or not it minimizes empirical risk. On the other hand, the unrestricted risk tends to zero as $m\to\infty$ for fixed $p,s,R,\sigma>0$, independently of $N$. Thus no growth of $N,S,B$ can make this original architecture attain the vanishing unrestricted risk along an odd-mesh subsequence. This is a partial resolution: no complete joint bounded-class rate, or corresponding fixed positive even-mesh floor, is asserted. The original question is retained verbatim under Original question.
items.axiom_use: No additional choice axiom is used; the laws, finite predictors and explicit constructions are supplied.
